Two related repos:
- andesim: /home/nick/work/andesim (branch andesim). Hybrid RISC-V simulator orchestration: C++ driver (driver/, ./andesim), QEMU TCG plugin (qemu_plugin/), runtime (runtime/), test harness (tests/, scripts/), docs.
- vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim. External vsim (SystemC+Verilator) with hybrid orchestration in src/hybrid/*.hpp, cmake/, tests/.

Known history (ground truth for what "legacy" means here — read CLAUDE.md at /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md and git log for detail):
- The QEMU2 handback leg was REMOVED: flow is now QEMU1 -> vsim, done. Any code/option/doc still implementing or describing a QEMU2 resume/ship-back step is legacy.
- vsim used to live in-tree under verilator/ in andesim; it moved to the external repo. Anything in andesim still referencing an in-tree verilator/ path, or building vsim locally, is legacy. NOTE: andesim/CLAUDE.md itself has a stale "vsim CMake Structure" section claiming "vsim lives entirely in verilator/" — stale docs count as findings.
- QEMU also moved to an external prebuilt (QEMU_BIN_DIR); anything cloning/building QEMU in-tree is legacy.
- Semihosting/libgloss_vh: nothing in-tree links -lgloss_vh anymore; the vplat runtime replaced it. BUT asm fixtures intentionally keep a semihosting exit fallback (semihost_exit.inc) — that is NOT legacy, per CLAUDE.md.
- The shell driver was replaced by the C++ ./andesim driver as the only user-facing driver; tests/e2e.sh is still the harness used internally (NOT legacy).

Rules:
- ONLY tracked files (git ls-files). Ignore untracked/gitignored files entirely.
- include/ in andesim is a git submodule (shared ABI pinned by BOTH repos) — never propose deletions inside it. Same for vsim external/ submodules.
- Do not propose deleting anything just because it looks old — you need positive evidence it is dead: unreferenced (grep both repos), superseded, or describes removed behavior.
- Check references across BOTH repos before claiming dead (vsim scripts may call andesim files and vice versa).
- Use git log --follow on suspicious files to understand their story.
Return findings as structured data. Be precise with paths and line ranges.

You are an adversarial verifier. A finder claims this is LEGACY code safe to delete. Try hard to REFUTE it.

Finding: repo=vsim path=src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp lines=69-72 kind=stale-doc
Claim: The encode_vle8_v comment says the PB reload sweep runs 'after a vsetvl to e8/m1', but the sweep has used e8/m8 (LMUL=8 grouped, 8 registers per vle8.v) since the transport was completed.
Evidence given: Same file: kVtypeE8M8 = 0xC3 'vtype encoding for e8, m8' (lines 169-172) and pb_v_data_sweep's leading vsetvl stages kVtypeE8M8 with kRegsPerGroup=8 and a static_assert tying vlmul to LMUL=8 (lines 209-228). Commit f6e869d 'feat(hybrid): V regfile transport, complete (v0..v31, LMUL=8 grouped sweep)' introduced the grouped sweep; resume_driver.hpp:192 correctly says '(e8/m8)'.

Repo roots: andesim=/home/nick/work/andesim, vsim=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim.
Checks you MUST do:
1. Read the file/lines yourself — does the claim match reality?
2. grep BOTH repos (tracked files) for references: filename, function names, symbols, script names, make targets, cmake targets, doc links.
3. Check tests/e2e.sh, scripts/*, Makefiles, CMake, and CLAUDE.md/docs for indirect usage (variable-built names, glob patterns like test_*.sh runners).
4. git log --follow -5 on the file: was it recently touched for a live feature?
5. Is it an INTENTIONAL fallback/compat layer per CLAUDE.md (e.g. semihost_exit.inc)?
If ANY live reference or intentional-keep reason exists, verdict isLegacy=false. Default to false when uncertain. If true, give the exact deleteScope.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

50	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
51	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
52	         | (0b111u << 12)
53	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
54	         | 0x57u;  // OP-V opcode
55	}
56	
57	// Encode `csrrw rd, csr, rs1` (SYSTEM opcode, funct3=001).
58	// Tier-A PB fallback: stage the CSR value in rs1 via Abstract Command,
59	// then write it to a CSR that the DM cannot reach via abstract access.
60	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_csrrw(uint8_t rd, uint16_t csr, uint8_t rs1)
61	{
62	    return ((uint32_t(csr) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
63	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
64	         | (0b001u << 12)
65	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
66	         | 0x73u;  // SYSTEM opcode
67	}
68	
69	// Encode `vle8.v vd, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector load, EEW=8 (RVV 1.0 sec 7.4).
70	// Fields: vm=1 (unmasked, bit 25), width=000, mop=00, mew=0, nf=000,
71	// lumop=00000, opcode LOAD-FP=0x07. PB V-regfile reload sweeps v0..v31 from
72	// the shared scratch region after a vsetvl to e8/m1.
73	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vle8_v(uint8_t vd, uint8_t rs1)
74	{
75	    return (1u << 25)
76	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
77	         | ((uint32_t(vd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
78	         | 0x07u;  // LOAD-FP opcode
79	}
80	
81	// Encode `vse8.v vs3, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector store, EEW=8. Mirror of
82	// encode_vle8_v with opcode STORE-FP=0x27. PB V-regfile dump sweeps v0..v31
83	// back to the shared scratch region at drain.
84	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vse8_v(uint8_t vs3, uint8_t rs1)
85	{
86	    return (1u << 25)
87	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
88	         | ((uint32_t(vs3) & 0x1Fu) << 7)
89	         | 0x27u;  // STORE-FP opcode
90	}
91	
92	// Encode `addi rd, rs1, imm12` (OP-IMM opcode 0x13, funct3=000). The batched
93	// V-data sweep advances the scratch base pointer x7 by one register-span
94	// between transfers WITHIN a Program-Buffer execution, so the per-register
95	// abstract x7 write disappears. imm12 is a signed 12-bit field (-2048..2047).
96	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_addi(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
97	{
98	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
99	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
100	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
101	         | 0x13u;  // OP-IMM opcode (funct3=000)
102	}
103	
104	// Encode `lwu rd, imm12(rs1)` (LOAD opcode 0x03, funct3=110 for 32-bit ZERO-
105	// extend, I-type). L2C MMIO registers must be accessed less than 8 bytes at a
106	// time (DS220 11.8.3), so the L2C config read-back loads a word. lwu (not lw)
107	// so a 32-bit register value does not sign-extend into the upper bits of the
108	// 64-bit GPR it lands in.
109	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_lwu(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
110	{
111	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
112	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
113	         | (0b110u << 12)
114	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
115	         | 0x03u;  // LOAD opcode
116	}
117	
118	// Encode `sw rs2, imm12(rs1)` (STORE opcode 0x23, funct3=010 for 32-bit,
119	// S-type: imm[11:5] -> bits 31:25, imm[4:0] -> bits 11:7). L2C MMIO registers
120	// must be accessed less than 8 bytes at a time (DS220 11.8.3), so the L2C
121	// config restore writes a word. All documented L2C control bits live in the
122	// low 32 bits.
123	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_sw(uint8_t rs2, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
124	{
125	    const uint32_t imm = uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu;
126	    return ((imm >> 5) & 0x7Fu) << 25
127	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
128	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
129	         | (0b010u << 12)
130	         | ((imm & 0x1Fu) << 7)
131	         | 0x23u;  // STORE opcode
132	}
133	
134	// Write insns[0..n-1] to progbuf0..n-1 and kEbreak to progbuf[n].
135	// Clears any sticky abstractcs.cmderr (W1C), issues kExecProgbufCmd, polls
136	// until abstractcs.busy clears, then verifies cmderr stayed clear.
137	//
138	// Throws std::runtime_error if insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns, if the poll
139	// times out, or if the DM raises cmderr during execution. No caller has a
140	// legitimate reason to silently continue on PB failure - the hart state
141	// would be partially restored / partially drained, which is worse than
142	// surfacing the fault.
143	template<typename Bus>
144	inline void exec_progbuf(Bus& bus, std::span<const uint32_t> insns)
145	{
146	    if (insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns)
147	        throw std::runtime_error(
148	            "exec_progbuf: too many instructions ("
149	            + std::to_string(insns.size()) + " > "
150	            + std::to_string(kProgbufMaxInsns) + ")");
151	
152	    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < insns.size(); ++i)
153	        bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + i), insns[i]);
154	    bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + insns.size()), kEbreak);
155	
156	    if ((bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask) != 0u)
157	        bus.write(kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsCmderrMask);
158	
159	    bus.write(kDmiCommand, kExecProgbufCmd);
160	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy, "exec_progbuf busy");
161	
162	    const uint32_t cmderr = bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask;
163	    if (cmderr != 0u)
164	        throw std::runtime_error(
165	            "exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr="
166	            + std::to_string(cmderr >> 8));
167	}
168	
169	// vtype encoding for e8, m8, ta, ma (vsew=000, vlmul=011, vta=1, vma=1). The
170	// V-data sweep uses LMUL=8 so one vle8.v/vse8.v moves a whole group of 8
171	// registers (8*vlenb byte-elements, vl=8*vlenb) in a single instruction.
172	inline constexpr uint32_t kVtypeE8M8 = 0xC3u;
173	
174	// Abstract-command write of a 64-bit value to Debug Module register `regno`
175	// (GPR/CSR/FPR): DATA0/DATA1 + Access-Register(write) + busy-poll. Free
176	// function so ResumeDriver, StateDrain, and the V-data sweep share one copy.
177	template<typename Bus>
178	inline void write_register_abstract(Bus& bus, uint16_t regno, uint64_t value)
179	{
180	    bus.write(kDmiData0, static_cast<uint32_t>(value & 0xffffffffu));
181	    bus.write(kDmiData1, static_cast<uint32_t>((value >> 32) & 0xffffffffu));
182	    bus.write(kDmiCommand,
183	              access_register_command(regno, AarSize::Bits64, /*write=*/true));
184	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy,
185	                     "write_register_abstract");
186	}
187	
188	// Sweep all 32 V data registers between the hart regfile and the vlenb-packed
189	// scratch region via the Program Buffer. load=true issues vle8.v
190	// (scratch -> regfile, on resume); load=false issues vse8.v (regfile ->
191	// scratch, at drain). The leading vsetvl to e8/m8 sets vl=8*vlenb and forces
192	// vstart=0, so one unit-stride access covers a whole LMUL=8 group of 8
193	// registers. Uses x5/x6 (vsetvl operands) and x7 (group base pointer) as
194	// scratch. `vlenb` is the runtime per-register width; the scratch must be
195	// packed at vlenb stride (stage_v_to_scratch) so each 8-register group is
196	// contiguous.
197	template<typename Bus>
198	inline void pb_v_data_sweep(Bus& bus, uint64_t scratch_gpa, uint64_t vlenb,
199	                            bool load)
200	{
201	    // The scratch holds v0..v31 packed contiguously at vlenb stride (see
202	    // stage_v_to_scratch), so 8 consecutive registers form one LMUL=8 group.
203	    // One vle8.v/vse8.v then moves a whole group (8*vlenb contiguous bytes,
204	    // vl=8*vlenb) and all 32 registers transfer in 4 grouped ops -- whose 4
205	    // (transfer; addi) pairs fit in a SINGLE Program-Buffer execution. Each PB
206	    // execution is one halted-hart DM round-trip (~1000 sim cycles in the
207	    // busy-poll), so this is the floor: one vsetvl + one grouped execution. The
208	    // register bytes never cross DMI; they ride the shared mmap.
209	    constexpr unsigned     kRegsPerGroup   = 8;  // LMUL=8
210	    // kVtypeE8M8's vlmul field (bits 2:0) must encode this LMUL, so one grouped
211	    // vle8.v/vse8.v really covers kRegsPerGroup registers (integer LMUL=1<<vlmul;
212	    // 0xC3 & 7 == 3 -> LMUL 8).
213	    static_assert((1u << (kVtypeE8M8 & 0x7u)) == kRegsPerGroup,
214	                  "kVtypeE8M8 must encode LMUL = kRegsPerGroup");
215	    constexpr std::size_t  kGroupSweepInsns = (32 / kRegsPerGroup) * 2;  // (ld;addi)*4
216	    static_assert(kGroupSweepInsns <= kProgbufMaxInsns,
217	                  "the grouped sweep must fit one Program Buffer execution");
218	    const uint64_t group_bytes = static_cast<uint64_t>(kRegsPerGroup) * vlenb;
219	    if (group_bytes > 2047)  // addi imm12 is signed 12-bit; max 8*128 = 1024
220	        throw std::runtime_error(
221	            "pb_v_data_sweep: 8*vlenb exceeds the addi imm12 range");
222	
223	    // vsetvl to e8/m8 with AVL = 8*vlenb sets vl = VLMAX = 8*vlenb (one
224	    // byte-element per lane across the whole group) and forces vstart = 0.
225	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(5), group_bytes);  // AVL
226	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(6), kVtypeE8M8);   // e8, m8, ta, ma
227	    const std::array<uint32_t, 1> pb_vsetvl = { encode_vsetvl(0, 5, 6) };
228	    exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{pb_vsetvl});
229	
230	    // Base pointer x7 staged once; the in-buffer addi advances it one group at
231	    // a time. The group base register must be LMUL-aligned: v0/v8/v16/v24.
232	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(7), scratch_gpa);
233	    const uint32_t addi_step =
234	        encode_addi(7, 7, static_cast<int32_t>(group_bytes));
235	    std::array<uint32_t, kGroupSweepInsns> group_sweep{};
236	    std::size_t n = 0;
237	    for (uint8_t g = 0; g < 32; g += kRegsPerGroup) {
238	        group_sweep[n++] = load ? encode_vle8_v(g, 7) : encode_vse8_v(g, 7);
239	        group_sweep[n++] = addi_step;  // last group's addi is harmless dead work

commit f6e869d25d2dcdb16945a6b07940b5c43955fe08
Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Wed Jul 8 14:55:31 2026 +0800

    feat(hybrid): V regfile transport, complete (v0..v31, LMUL=8 grouped sweep)
    
    Completes the V-data transport prototyped in the previous commit. pb_v_data_sweep now moves all 32 registers: encode_addi advances the group base pointer x7 in-buffer and an LMUL=8 vtype (kVtypeE8M8) groups 8 registers per vle8.v/vse8.v, so the whole regfile transfers in one vsetvl plus one grouped Program-Buffer execution (kGroupSweepInsns, static_asserts pin the grouping), the perf floor for a halted-hart sweep. stage_v_to_scratch/read_v_from_scratch pack and unpack all 32 slots at the runtime vlenb stride so each 8-register group is contiguous. The reload sweep runs before the architectural V-CSR restore and the dump sweep runs last at drain, so neither can corrupt captured state. A V handoff that reaches either sweep with the scratch GPA still unset now throws instead of transporting through a bogus address. This completes v-data-transport (minimal was v0 only).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
